messages:
alex: Heads-up - after OFED 5.8.1 rollout to ap-east1 GPU pool we are seeing huge NCCL slowdowns and occasional fallbacks to TCP. 16-node allreduce latencies jumped 3-4x. :eyes:

maria: Confirming. ap-east1-gpu-32 shows repeated CQ timeouts in dmesg and mlx5 resets. Sample from node-32: ```mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: cq err on 0x3: rq_cqe_timeout, resetting qp```

jake: Link to job traces: https://internal.logs/redwood/ap-east1/trace/20789/job-1145 - you can see NCCL switching transports mid-run (ib -> tcp).

linh: Quick test: exporting NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on a replica restores progress (no CQ errors) but throughput is down ~60% (tcp fallback). Not acceptable for critical production jobs.

kevin: This looks like mlx5 firmware + OFED interaction. Release notes for the vendor firmware mention "CQ moderation changes" in 24.3 which can surface as CQE timeouts with high small-packet rates.

alex: Who rolled OFED? sre-bot: show rollout metadata.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: OFED 5.8.1 staged to ap-east1 (gpupool-1..4) at 2026-03-14T02:01Z by infra-cd pipeline. Canary passed synthetic p2p tests but not long-running NCCL allreduce.

maria: Canary test only ran 2-node p2p. Problem only shows up at >8 ranks under sustained allreduce. That slipped through.

ops-oncall: Starting a canary rollback on ap-east1-canary-1 now. I'll patch the rest to hold.

jake: Runtime log snippet from failed job: ```NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed: Invalid argument
NCCL WARN Transport (IB) error, falling back to TCP
NCCL INFO Using TCP transport for rank 3```

linh: Short-term mitigation options: 1) set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 globally (quick but big perf hit) 2) tweak mlx5 driver params (cq moderation, rx polling) 3) downgrade OFED/firmware (rollback).

kevin: Downgrade plan: rollback OFED to 5.7 on canary and run 16/32 node allreduce suites for 2 hours. If stable, schedule phased rollback. Need approval window for node reboots (some long-running customer jobs).

alex: Impact estimate: if we leave current state, average GPU job runtime +20-40% on allreduce-heavy workloads => effective capacity drop ~15% in ap-east1 during peak. That could cause queued jobs and cost overruns as we spin up extra capacity.

maria: Notify CS: some customers will see prolonged batch training. I'll draft a short note explaining rollback plan and ETA.

ops-oncall: Canary rollback finished on ap-east1-canary-1 at 02:46Z. Running 32-node allreduce now.

sre-bot: health-check: ap-east1-gpupool-1/2/3 status: degraded (packet drops, retries). ap-east1-canary-1: stable after rollback (no cq errors in last 15m).

jake: Can we capture NIC-level counters for the failing nodes (rx_cqe_err, qp_retries) and compare to canary? That will make forensics easier.

maria: Collected counters and attached to ticket #INFRA-4821. Early diff: failing nodes show qp_retry_exceeded and increased RNR_NAKs. See gist: https://internal.gists/infra/4821-counters

kevin: Also check kernel ABI mismatch possibility with new ofed stack. Some kernels shipped with slightly different libibverbs ABI and that can cause subtle failures under load.

linh: Action items: 
- [ops-oncall] finish canary validation (run 2h long-run test)
- [maria] notify CS and post-mortem stub
- [kevin] prepare rollback playbook and coordinate maintenance windows
- [jake] gather counters + attach perf graphs and logs to INFRA-4821

alex: If canary is good, hold global rollout and run extended tests in eu and us fleets before redeploy. No autopromote.

ops-oncall: Canary 32-node test passed at 04:20Z. No CQ timeouts. I'll schedule a phased rollback tonight 23:00-02:00 UTC to minimize customer impact.

maria: Thx. CS notified for tonight's window. Also flagging cost ops: if rollback takes longer, we might need short-term extra spot capacity in other regions to soak queue, estimate 5-10% additional spend for 24-48h.

alex: Good catch team. Follow-up: we should add a long-run NCCL allreduce test to the rollout gate and add NIC counters as a canary signal.

jake: I'll open a PR to infra-cd with the updated gate and alerts.

kevin: Also let's file a vendor bug w/ vendor FW logs and request root-cause analysis for the CQ moderation change.

linh: Marking thread resolved for now. We have rollback plan + CS comms + test gate. Will keep monitoring. :white_check_mark:
